transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for letting me know. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your surgery, it's safe to continue using them now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thank you. I'm also experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Some sensitivity to light is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, wearing sunglasses when you go outside should help.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. 

Are you experiencing severe pain, or is it just mild sensitivity?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It's just mild sensitivity to bright light, and it feels quite manageable. I've been wearing sunglasses, and it seems to help. I do have one more question. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's good to hear the sunglasses are helping!

Regarding blurriness - it's quite common for vision not to be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text:
My surgery was a couple of weeks ago, and the blurriness is a bit better than right after the surgery. It's reassuring to hear that it's normal for it to take a little time. 

And no, I don't have any more questions. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's great to hear that your vision is improving - that's exactly what we'd expect at a couple of weeks post-surgery.

So just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you so much for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and remember to keep wearing those sunglasses outside.

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` and `mild_case_advice` in the turn starting with "Some sensitivity to light is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens." It also conveyed `escalation_criteria` in the same turn by stating, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further." All points were covered.
